meta.title: Philosophy
meta.description: Read about Happy Hacking Space, a network of hackers. We want to make building apps and websites accessible to everyone.

superpower.title: Coding is a
superpower.description: Learning to code is uniquely like gaining a superpower: it converts you from a consumer to a creator. Suddenly, computers become a tool for creating.

makeFromAnywhere.title: Make, from anywhere.
makeFromAnywhere.description: There's never been a better time for making: anywhere in the world, anyone with a laptop and an internet connection can learn to make an app. Building things has never been so globally democratized.

hackHackHack.title: Hack, hack, hack.
hackHackHack.description: The goal of Happy Hacking Space is to help you become a hacker. We want a space at every place where people are making interesting things with code, every week. Schools or institutions don't provide that, so we're creating it in every place to make building things accessible to everyone.

startBuilding.title: Start building.
startBuilding.description: Most coding classes teach you programming concepts instead of how to write real code—it's like trying to learn carpentry without any wood. So at Happy Hacking Space, you learn to code entirely through building things. You start with no experience and build and ship a project every meeting.

learnAsYouBuild.title: Learn as you build.
learnAsYouBuild.description1: Just as the best carpenters didn't learn in the classroom, neither did the best programmers. Through our
learnAsYouBuild.description2: , you'll be walked through building projects. Starting out, you won't understand how the code works, but you'll build understanding as you go. You'll get stuck along the way, but we're here to help.

community.title: Be part of a community.
community.description: Happy Hacking Space gives you a community of thousands of other makers to talk to. We're artists, writers, engineers, tinkerers, campers, filmmakers, volunteers. We make things. We help one another. We have fun. Join us.

vision.nextTenYears: In the next ten years, Happy Hacking Space will discover, foster and inspire thousands more to use technical skills to solve problems.
vision.ledBy: Led by hackers, crafters, explorers, Happy Hacking Space already reaches thousands, and represents the largest technical network in the Mesopotamia. Each day, new projects are shipped, new lines of code are written, and new friendships are forged through collaborative, problem-solving technical projects happening at Happy Hacking Space.
vision.alwaysFree: Happy Hacking Space is always free for hackers and with your support, Happy Hacking Space can grow to hundreds of thousands of hackers, bringing free computer science education, a hacker mindset, and an equal shot at success to every hacker, regardless of where they're from, how they identify, or what their parents do.
vision.overTime: Over time, Happy Hackers will reshape societies as entrepreneurs, environmentalists, political leaders, activists and policy makers. We help shape the values of these future leaders, modeling and incentivizing them to be curious, humble, kind, optimistic problem solvers.
vision.needSupport: We need your support to make this vision a reality.

meta.title: Don't Ask to Ask — Question Asking Guide
meta.description: A guide to asking questions efficiently in the Happy Hacking Space community.

hero.title: For Quick Answers: A Guide to Asking Questions
hero.subtitle: Save time and keep the community productive.

dontasktoask.intro: At Happy Hacking Space, we follow this approach to save time and keep the community productive:

section1.title: Don't Ask "Can I Ask a Question?", Just Ask
section1.description: Instead of intros like "Is anyone available?" or "Can I ask something?", write the topic, what you've tried, and the error you got — all in one message.

section2.title: Example: Time Waster vs. Hacker Method

bad.line1: Hey, is there anyone who knows Python?
bad.line3: I'm getting an error, can we look at it?
bad.line4: Sure, what's the error? Can you send the code?
bad.line5: [Sends photo of code] Look, it says NameError here.
bad.line6: It's hard to read from a photo, but it looks like you didn't define the variable...
bad.result: Result: 50 minutes spent on a simple fix.

good.line1: Hey, I'm getting a NameError in Python while printing a list. I defined the variable but it's not seeing it. Here's my code, can you help? my_list = [1, 2, 3] print(my_lista)
good.line2: Hey Arjin, you wrote the variable name wrong in print, there's an extra 'a' at the end.
good.result: Result: Problem solved in 2 minutes, everyone got back to work!

section3.title: Whatever the Topic, Ask in a "Package"
section3.description: Whether it's a software bug, design idea, or hardware issue; always include these in a single message:

goal.title: Goal:
goal.desc: What are you trying to do?

attempt.title: Attempt:
attempt.desc: What have you tried so far?

error.title: Error:
error.desc: Where exactly are you stuck? (Add error code, image, or link.)

section4.title: Don't Send Photos, Share
section4.description: Use code blocks for code, and clear visuals for design or hardware issues.

summary.title: In Short
summary.text: The better you package your problem, the faster you can get back to hacking.
